metaTitle: Best Wireless Charger Alarm Clocks in 2026
metaDescription: Five alarm clocks with built-in wireless charging compared on digit size, dimming, radio and Bluetooth extras, and how easy each is to set up.
introParagraphs: A wireless charger alarm clock puts the phone, the time, and the alarm in one spot, which cuts nightstand clutter and the fumbling for a cable in the dark. The five picks here share that idea but diverge on extras. The iHome adds a Bluetooth speaker, the ANJANK adds an FM radio, and the DreamSky, Andoolex, and URAYCO lean on wood finishes and large displays.

The spread is easy to see. The DreamSky lists 1.8 inch digits on a 6.5 inch clock with 5 brightness levels and an off mode, the ANJANK supports 5W, 7.5W, and 10W adaptive charging, and the URAYCO offers 0 to 99% dimming. We ranked the DreamSky first because its large digits and off mode matter more at night than any extra feature.

This guide is based on product specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on testing, and it does not quote prices. Wireless charging in a clock is usually 10W or less, and thick cases cut efficiency. Use the criteria below to decide which extras are worth having.

products.name: DreamSky Wooden Digital Alarm Clock with Wireless Charging
products.description:
The DreamSky is the clock for anyone who wants to read the time without glasses. The listing gives 1.8 inch digits on a 6.5 inch wooden body, and says setup is simple. It includes a 10W wireless pad on top, which is a reasonable tier for a bedside unit.

The dimmer is the practical highlight. It has 5 brightness levels plus an OFF mode, so you can black out the display at night while still charging. The tradeoff is that it lacks a radio or speaker, and the 10W tier is lower than a separate 15W pad.

It wipes clean, though wood may show scratches. Compared with the ANJANK, it focuses on readability. Against the iHome, it skips Bluetooth.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants big digits and a display that can go fully dark.
pros: 1.8 inch digits are easy to read
5 brightness levels plus an OFF mode
Wood housing looks good on a nightstand

products.name: iHome Bluetooth Alarm Clock with Wireless Charger

specList.label: Time
specList.value: Syncs to phone time via Bluetooth

products.description:
The iHome is the most feature-rich pick. It combines a wireless charger, a USB charging port, a digital alarm clock, and a Bluetooth speaker with streaming range of up to 100 feet. It syncs the clock time to the phone over Bluetooth, which means no manual setting.

The tradeoff is complexity. More features mean more buttons and menus to learn, and the listing leaves out the wireless wattage. It is also the highest-priced pick in this guide.

It works as a bedroom speaker for podcasts and audiobooks. Compared with the DreamSky, it adds audio but skips wood styling. Against the ANJANK, it adds Bluetooth instead of FM radio.
products.bestFor: People who want a speaker and automatic time sync.
pros: Clock syncs to phone time automatically
USB port for a second device

products.name: ANJANK Wooden Digital Alarm Clock with FM Radio
products.description:
The ANJANK is a 3 in 1 clock, FM radio, and wireless charger. It is Qi certified with adaptive 5W, 7.5W, and 10W charging, and the radio covers 87.5 to 108MHz with saved channels. A sleep timer lets you fall asleep to the radio.

The tradeoff is that the radio needs an antenna position that works in your home, and the listing does not give digit size. The wood body is attractive but the controls take a moment to learn.

It wipes clean. Compared with the iHome, it offers radio instead of Bluetooth. Against the DreamSky, it has more features but less clarity on readability.
products.bestFor: Radio listeners who fall asleep to the sound.

products.name: Andoolex Premium Brown Wooden Alarm Clock
products.description:
The Andoolex is a wood grain clock with a built-in fast wireless pad for Qi phones and dual USB-A ports. It is positioned as an all-in-one charging station to eliminate cables. The oversized LED shows real-time and date, with dual alarms and sleep functions.

The tradeoff is that the listing is heavy on marketing language and light on wattage. The wood veneer looks good but may show scratches. Dual USB-A ports are useful, but only if your devices still use that connector.

It wipes clean. Compared with the URAYCO, it is nearly the same concept at a higher tier. Against the DreamSky, it adds ports but less clarity on digit size.
products.bestFor: Households that charge a phone and other devices overnight.
pros: Wireless pad plus dual USB-A ports
cons: Wattage is not stated in the listing

products.name: URAYCO Premium Wooden Digital Alarm Clock
products.description:
The URAYCO is the lowest-cost pick and covers the basics well. It has a wireless charging pad, dual USB ports, dual alarms, and a snooze function. The display dims from 0 to 99%, so it can go fully dark, and a DST function adjusts for daylight saving time.

The tradeoff is detail. The listing does not give wireless wattage or digit size. Wood grain texture adds style, but the listing leans on marketing language.

It wipes clean and sets up quickly. Compared with the Andoolex, it costs less. Against the DreamSky, it offers a finer dimmer but fewer readability details.
products.bestFor: A budget clock with dimming that goes fully dark.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The DreamSky lists 1.8 inch digits on a 6.5 inch clock, which is easy to read without glasses. Other listings share no size. A small display defeats the point of a bedside clock. Check digit size before buying.
A bright display can wake a sleeper. The DreamSky has 5 brightness levels plus OFF, and the URAYCO dims from 0 to 99%. Look for an option that goes dark. Light matters more at night.
The DreamSky lists 10W and the ANJANK supports 5W, 7.5W, and 10W adaptive charging. Others do not state wattage. Wireless in a clock is usually 10W or less. Overnight charging does not need more.
The iHome adds a Bluetooth speaker with a range of up to 100 feet, and the ANJANK adds an FM radio. Extras add buttons. Pick the extras you will use. Otherwise a simple clock is easier.
Cases of about 3 mm or thinner work through most chargers, while thick cases cut efficiency. Wallet cases are a problem. Place the phone in the center of the pad. Remove the case if charging fails.
The Andoolex and URAYCO include dual USB ports, and the iHome includes a USB port. Check that the ports match your devices. A clock with ports can replace a power strip. Count your devices.

howWeEvaluated.title: Readability
howWeEvaluated.description: The DreamSky lists 1.8 inch digits and an OFF mode, which is the strongest. The others share less.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated wireless wattage. The DreamSky lists 10W and the ANJANK lists adaptive 5W to 10W. Others are vague.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: The iHome adds Bluetooth, the ANJANK adds radio, and the Andoolex and URAYCO add USB ports. Extras matter only if used.

howWeEvaluated.title: Setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at ease of setup. The iHome syncs time over Bluetooth, and the DreamSky says setup takes two steps. Easy setup scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what each pick offers for its price tier without quoting numbers. The URAYCO is the lowest-cost pick and the iHome the highest.

faq.q: What is the best wireless charger alarm clock?
faq.a: The DreamSky is the best overall for its large digits and OFF display mode. The iHome is the pick for Bluetooth audio. The URAYCO is the lowest-cost clock.

faq.q: Does wireless charging in a clock work with a case?
faq.a: Cases of about 3 mm or thinner usually work. Thick cases cut efficiency. Remove the case if charging fails.
Most are 10W or less. The DreamSky lists 10W and the ANJANK supports up to 10W. Overnight charging does not need more.

faq.q: Can I turn the display off?
faq.a: The DreamSky has an OFF mode and the URAYCO dims to 0%. That is useful for sleep. Check the dimmer before buying.

faq.q: Do I need Bluetooth or radio?
faq.a: Only if you will use them. The iHome has Bluetooth and the ANJANK has FM radio. Otherwise a simple clock is easier.
They can show scratches. Wipe with a soft cloth. Avoid damp cloths.
Chargers with overheat protection are designed for it. Keep metal off the pad. Choose a clock with a dim display.
